en: Using a ramp to load a heavy box reduces the lifting force needed, preventing back injuries.
Wearing rubber-soled shoes increases friction with the floor, preventing you from slipping on wet surfaces.
Storing heavy objects on high shelves is dangerous because gravity will accelerate them downward if they fall.
The strong magnetic field of neodymium magnets can permanently erase credit card data and disrupt pacemaker functions.
Water conducts electricity, so touching a plugged-in appliance with wet hands can cause a fatal electric shock.
Staring directly at a solar eclipse without certified eclipse glasses can cause permanent damage to your retina.
Listening to music through headphones at volumes above 85 decibels for extended periods causes permanent hearing loss.
Metal pot handles become hot because heat transfers from the boiling water inside the pot through conduction.
A moving bicycle possesses kinetic energy, which is why wearing a helmet protects your head during a crash.
A knife acts as a wedge to concentrate force, so you must always cut away from your body to avoid severe lacerations.
Plugging too many appliances into one extension cord causes overheating because the circuit draws more current than the wires can safely handle.
Using a dry, thick cloth to hold a hot pan works because the trapped air acts as a thermal insulator.
